title: Nonlinear vibration analysis of the high-efficiency compressive-mode piezoelectric energy harvester
venue: Proceedings of SPIE, the International Society for Optical Engineering/Proceedings of SPIE

sections.heading: Nonlinear vibration analysis of the high-efficiency compressive-mode piezoelectric energy harvester
sections.text: Zhengbao Yang and Jean Zu Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, University of Toronto Toronto, Ontario, Canada, M5S 3G8

sections.heading: ABSTRACT
sections.text:
Power source is critical to achieve independent and autonomous operations of electronic mobile devices. The vibration-based energy harvesting is extensively studied recently, and recognized as a promising technology to realize inexhaustible power supply for small-scaleelectronics.Among various approaches, the piezoleic energyharvestin has gaine the most attention due toits hig conversion efficiency and simple congurations. However, most of piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) to date are based on bending-beam structures and can only generate limited power with a narrow working bandwidth. The insufient electricoutput has grealy impeded their practical applications. In this paper, we present an innovative lead zirconate titanate (PZT) energy harvester, named high-eficiency compressive-mode piezoelectric energy harvester (HC-PEH), to enhance the performanceofenergy harvesters.A theoretical model was developed analytically, and solvednumerically to study the nonlinear characteristics of the HC-PEH. The results estimated by the developed mode agree well with the experimental data from the fabricated prototype. The HC-PEH shows strong nonlinear responses, favorable working bandwidth and superior power output. Under a weak excitation of 0.3 g $\mathrm { \overrightarrow { g } } = 9 . 8 ~ m / s ^ { 2 }$ ), a maximum power output 30 mW is generated at 22 Hz, which is about ten times better than current energy harvesters. The HC-PEH demonstrates the capability of generating enough power for most of wireless sensors.

Keywords: Energy harvester, Piezoelectric, High-efficiency, Compressive mode, Force amplification, Flextensional.

sections.heading: 1. INTRODUCTION
sections.text:
In the past decade, theenergy harvestingtechnology hasattracteconsiderableattention bot academiaand indusrywing ts reat application potentialTakethe rapid developing wireless senor network or exaple. Sensor nodes are being popularly employed in a variety of areas, including structural health monitoring $^ { 1 - 3 }$ forest fre monitoring,railay system, etReplacin r recharging batteris or largenumber  snsors ine area is very costly and time-consuming. Therefore, a device that can scavenge ambient vibration as a long lasting power source becomes a loadstone. Energy harvesters can also be applied in medical devices such as artificial pacemakers,6 spinal simulators7 and hearing aids $^ 8$ to lower their dependence on batteries and prolong their effective life span.

Among different mechanisms of harvesting vibration energy to date, piezoelectric mechanism is the most promising one due to its simple configurations and high power density. Nevertheless, piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) have also demonstrated several critical issues. These shortcomings are tethered to their innate operating concept. Currently, most of PEHs are employing the cantilever structure or modifed bendingbeam structures. $^ { 9 - 1 1 }$ Although the beam structures can induce large bending strains under weak vibrations with simple confgurations, they sur from the low power output and cannot generate enough electricity for mosto elecronics.1 In addition, the most commonly-used cantilevered PEHs can only convert energy from excitations to electric loads effectively in a narrow frequency region around the fundamental frequency.Small variations in the excitation requency will render the vibration away rom resonance, resulting in a sinificant drop  the output. The narrow bandwidth makes PEHs impracticable in the ambient random vibrating environment. These critical issues have greatly impeded the extensive adoption of the energy harvesting technology.

It shows strong nonlinear responses, wide working bandwidth and high power output. In this paper, the electrical-mechanical coupling system is modeled analytically and examined numerically. Furthermore, a prototype was fabricated and tested.Theresults from experiments correlate we wit the data estimated by the mel and validate the superiority f the new HC-EH. This paper isorganized as follows: Section I presents the design of the HC-PEH, and the corresponding finite element analysis. Section III and Section IV show the modeling method and experiments, respectively. Results and discussions folow in Section V, and conclusions are provided in Section VI.

sections.heading: 3. THEORETICAL ANALYSIS
sections.text:
Avibration-based energyharvester using piezoelectricmaterials includes both mechanical and electrical domans, and can be modeled as either an equivalent spring-mass-damper system $^ { 1 4 , 1 5 }$ or an equivalent circuit system. $^ { 1 6 , 1 7 }$ Here we model the system as an equivalent circuit system as shown in Fig. 3. Since weak excitations are used in the study, the nonlinear piezoelectricity is $^ { 1 8 }$ not considered in the model. The piezoelectric materials are asumed linear, complying with the constitutive equations.19 In the system, force in the mechanical domain coon tovoltagetheelectrilmain; and velociyhemechaniloma corepon tcin the electrical domain. The energy storageelements mass and spring correspond to inductance and capacitance, respectively ( $l = m$ ; $c = 1 / k$ ). The energy dissipation element damping corresponds to resistance ( $R = c$ ). The electromechanical coupling is represented by a transformer with a turn-ratio $\theta$ $C _ { p }$ is the equivalent internal capacitance of the piezoelectric plate, and $R$ is the external load.

According to the Kirchhoff's circuit law, the governing equations are derived as:

$$
\begin{array} { c } { { m X ^ { \prime \prime } + c X ^ { \prime } + k _ { 1 } X + k _ { 3 } X ^ { 3 } + \theta V = m Z ^ { \prime \prime } } } \\ { { { } } } \\ { { C _ { p } V ^ { \prime } + \displaystyle { \frac { 1 } { R } } V = \theta X ^ { \prime } } } \end{array}
$$

The excitation is assumed to be a harmonic vibration:

$$
Z ^ { \prime \prime } = A \cos \omega t
$$

where $A$ is the acceleration amplitude, and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

sections.heading: 6. SUMMARY
sections.text:
This paper reports a new nonlinear energy harvester using compressive-mode piezoelectric materials. A concise lumped-parameter model was developed analytically and solved numerically. The model is capable of precisely estimating the nonlinear large-amplitude responses of the electromechanical coupling system. The vablity of introducing nonlinearity into energy harvesters to broaden the bandwidth is also verifed theoretically and experimentally. As the microelectronics technology develops rapidly, a variety of low-power sensors ( $< ~ 1$ milliwatt) have emerged. The superior performance of the HC-PEH gives an optimistic outlook for success in the endeavor of achieving self-powered wireless sensor networks.

The performance of the HC-PEH can be improved further by employing better active materials (e.g. PMN-PT) and optimizing the geometric parameters. A frequency-varying complex impedance matching methodology is also required to maximize the energy extraction, as mentioned before. Meanwhile, since the response of a nonlinear electrical-mechanical coupling system is nonlinear and quite complicated under the ambient random vibrating environment, comprehensive power management and storage strategies are of high value, and need more thorough and intensive research.
